audit.whatIsWrong: The page's central claim is that Riven dashes THROUGH Nevermove to dodge it — stated in whys[2] ('can sidestep your E hand mid-travel'), spikes[0].text ('close the gap through your E hand before it lands'), content.early ('she will dash through the hand's travel path') and wants.foe[0] ('Use Q triple-dash to sidestep your E hand'). The outgoing wave does not root at all.
audit.why: Riot's E text: 'Swain launches a wave of demonic power forward. It THEN RETURNS to Swain and roots enemies it hits.' The root is on the return sweep. Dashing through the outgoing wave achieves nothing — she is still on the wrong side when it comes back. This inverts the advice completely: the page tells the player to throw E only when her dashes are gone, when the correct read is to throw it so the RETURN catches her while she is committed. The mirror flagged the identical error from Riven's side and called it the biggest correction on that page: 'following that advice puts you exactly where the root catches you.'
audit.corrected: All four fields plus wants.you[0] and the tldr rewritten around the return sweep.

audit.whatIsWrong: Chart rows 0, 3, 4 and 6 disagreed with the packet and the mirror in both layers.
audit.why: packet.levelChart is Riven x6 then Skill, and the mirror set rows 0, 3, 4 to Riven and row 6 to Skill. The prose agrees on every one: whys[0] 'she wins any level-1 skirmish outright', whys[3] 'She zones you off fragments', whys[4] 'she can blow your health bar before your R drain accumulates', and whys[6] 'making outcome skill-dependent on execution' — which is the definition of a Skill row, not a Riven row. Rows 1, 2 and 5 already read Riven.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 3, 4 to Riven and row 6 to Skill in both layers as one atomic group. Row 6's existing 5/10 already suits Skill so it was left alone; rows 0, 3, 4 rescaled.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[1] calls Ki Burst 'a point-and-click setup'. It is not targeted.
audit.why: Riot's W text: 'Riven emits a Ki Burst, damaging and stunning nearby enemies' — a 260-range area burst centred on herself, on 11/10/9/8/7s. Calling it point-and-click tells the reader there is no spacing answer, when 260 units is in fact the whole answer. Nothing on the page carried its range or cooldown either.
audit.corrected: whys[1], dosFull[0].d, breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].t now state the 260 range and the 11s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three phase whys were boilerplate, and phases[4].why said 'Demonic Ascension turns his all-in into your healing' at level 6 — directly contradicting whys[4] and spikes[1] on the same page, which both say Blade of the Exile can kill you before the drain heals anything.
audit.why: Blade of the Exile grants Attack Damage and Range for a window and unlocks a single Wind Slash, on 120/90/60s. Level 6 is her spike here, not Swain's. Valor is a dash plus damage block on 10/9/8/7/6s and appears nowhere on the page despite being what eats the opener. Broken Wings is one 13s cooldown covering all three strikes, with the third knocking back — the page never says the three strikes share a cooldown, which is exactly what a player needs to count.
audit.corrected: phases[0], [3], [4], [6] rewritten; dosFull[2].d, dontsFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d now carry Broken Wings, Blade of the Exile and Valor with their numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Riven's ultimate carries the projectile flag, meaning Wind Slash is blockable by Wind Wall-class effects and spell shields.
audit.why: Not actionable for Swain — he has neither — so per the relevance rule I did not write it to the page. Recording it because it is a real cross-matchup fact the mirror also noticed, and it belongs on the pages of champions who can use it.

edits.before: Riven has everything you do not at levels 1-2: raw burst, two dashes, and a stun that can interrupt your E mid-cast. Do not throw E at a Riven who still has Q charges — she will dash through the hand's travel path and punish you inside your own minimum Q range. Play at max auto range, last-hit safely, and accept that she wins any trade you start before level 3. If she walks up aggressively, your Q burst at max range is your only deterrent; do not fish for E.
edits.after: Riven has everything you do not at levels 1-2: raw burst, two dashes, and a stun that can interrupt your E mid-cast. Do not throw E at a Riven who still has Broken Wings charges — the outgoing wave does not root, so she simply spends her dashes and is long gone before the return sweep. Play at max auto range, last-hit safely, and accept that she wins any trade you start before level 3. If she walks up aggressively, your Q burst at max range is your only deterrent; do not fish for E.

notes: The return-pass error on this page is the same defect the mirror found, and it is worth treating as a template-level bug rather than a Riven-specific one: every Swain page I audited in this slice describes Nevermove as a thing that lands where you throw it. It happens to be harmless wording against a stationary champion and actively wrong against every dash. A grep for 'E hand', 'dash through' and 'sidestep your E' across the Swain content file would probably find more.
